body:
## Summary

`clean --tier safe` removed the whole npx cache (`~/.npm/_npx`) while about ten processes were executing from it. One of them was disk-space-saviour itself, started with `npx disk-space-saviour@latest`. The run then stopped partway: 17 of the 28 planned items were processed, no summary was printed, and the audit log was left without `finishedAt`.

## Environment

- macOS (Darwin 24.6.0, Apple Silicon), Node 20.19.4
- `npx -y disk-space-saviour@latest`, which resolved to 0.13.1 (npm's `latest`). The repository's `main` is 0.14.0.

## Reproduction

1. Have long-running npx processes, for example MCP servers started as `npm exec @playwright/mcp@latest`. Here they ran from `~/.npm/_npx/9833c18b2d85bc59/node_modules/.bin/playwright-mcp`; `pgrep -fl playwright-mcp` showed 10 processes.
2. Run `npx -y disk-space-saviour@latest clean ~ /private/tmp --tier safe --yes`. dss itself then runs from `~/.npm/_npx/be59a9a24d743054/node_modules/.bin/dss`.
3. The dry run had already planned `npx-cache /Users/konard/.npm/_npx` (263 MiB) in the safe tier.

## Observed

- The audit log (`~/.local/state/disk-space-saviour/audit/dss-clean-…-22887.json`) records `npx-cache` `/Users/konard/.npm/_npx` with status `removed`, `deletedPaths: ["/Users/konard/.npm/_npx"]`, freed 276246528 bytes and no `skippedPaths`.
- After that entry the run recorded nothing more: 17 entries of the 28 planned, and `finishedAt` is `null`. The remaining safe items (Homebrew cache, VS Code `CachedData`, Yandex caches, pip, composer, rust-script, the Docker build cache, the node compile cache) were never processed.
- No summary was printed on stdout or stderr.
- The running MCP servers lost their package directory. They keep running from memory but can fail on the next lazy `require`.

## Expected

- A package directory under `~/.npm/_npx/<hash>` that holds the executable or the working directory of a running process is busy, and is skipped with a reason. The same goes for `bunx` (`$TMPDIR/bunx-*`), `pnpm dlx` and `yarn dlx` caches.
- dss never deletes the package it is running from. If it does, it reports the failure instead of exiting silently, and the audit log records the abort.
- The busy check should read process executables and open files (`lsof +D` or `/proc/*/exe`), not only process names. The npx rule's busy list names `npx`, but the processes here run as `node …/_npx/<hash>/…`.
- Removal should go per entry: remove `_npx/<hash>` directories that are idle, rather than the whole `_npx` root.

## Severity

This is a correctness and safety bug in the default (safe) tier: it breaks running tools and aborts the cleanup run.
title: Safe tier deletes the npx cache under running processes, including dss itself, and the run aborts silently
